idea: Development appraisal modelling for small developers
pain: Appraisals built badly in Excel; finance conversations go poorly
v1: One appraisal model for one live site
verdict: Real fit and real pain, but the buyer is one hop away and pays project fees rather than retainers.

why.distribution: Her architects know developers; that is a hop, and developers are not her own relationships.
why.demand: Developers do pay consultants for appraisals; the category exists.
why.fmf: Financial modelling plus genuine understanding of what gets built - unusually well matched.
why.revenue_structure: Site by site, repeating only when the developer has a new scheme.
why.defensibility: Quantity surveyors and development consultants already do this.
why.leverage: Templates help substantially but each site needs her judgement.
why.time_to_revenue: An architect introduction to a live site in 1-3 months.
why.tailwind: UK small-scale development is constrained by rates and planning.
why.ceiling: £4.5k x 30 sites = £135k, and 30 sites means many developer relationships she does not yet have.

ceiling_arithmetic: £4.5k x 30 sites = £135k. Each developer brings 2-3 sites a year at most, so 30 sites needs 10-15 developer relationships built from introductions. Realistic year one: 6-10 sites = £27-45k.
carries: Genuine two-domain fit and a pain developers feel acutely when seeking finance.
kills: Ceiling. Fees are too low and the relationship count required is too high for a part-time founder.
test: Ask three architect contacts to introduce a developer client with a live site.
test_pass: One developer pays for an appraisal.
test_fail: Introductions happen but nobody has budget.
